abilities.name: Savvy Strategy: Splitting the Spoils
abilities.caveat: Shadow Pursuit ends when (a) the user re-presses E (drain flask), (b) the user starts an N or Aim action (also drains flask), (c) the flask is full and discharges, or (d) the 5.57s max duration runs out. The planner only models case (d) — the early-exit cases produce a different drained-flask hit (filled vs unfilled). Authoring requires an `afterAction` trigger primitive the schema lacks. Filled vs unfilled flask DMG and the Moonsign Ascendant Gleam Meowball volley (which fires the absorbed element instead of Anemo) are not separately modeled.
_curatorNotes: Tap E (out-of-stance): dash + enter Shadow Pursuit at +30f (skillWindup). Max stance duration = shadowPursuitMaxDuration=334f = 5.57s. behavior:stance + opensState:inStance + terminatesOnSwap:true matches the swap-exit case.

Cooldown: SetCD(skill, skillCD+skillWindup) = (15+0.5)*60 = 15.5s starting at stance end (called inside cancelPursuit). With behavior:stance + duration:5.57 + cooldown:15.5, the parser counts cooldown after duration ends — total cycle = 5.57s stance + 15.5s cd = 21.07s.
Frames: skillFrames=InitAbilSlice(12+30=42) — no explicit overrides, all keys=42. Per E-spec swap/N/Q/D/J authored uniformly.

Flask absorption: during stance, scans every 29f (fillFlaskInterval) for Pyro/Hydro/Electro/Cryo aura on enemy; first match locks the flask element, subsequent matches of same element fill the gauge by 25 each (max 100). Flask state isn't modeled.

On stance exit (re-press E or NA/Aim or duration-end): drainFlask fires either filledFlask (212% Anemo at lvl=10) if gauge=100, or unfilledFlask (190.8% Anemo at lvl=10). Single-element absorption + gauge tracking are deferred primitives.

Moonsign Ascendant Gleam: with full flask, Meowballs fire instead of unfilled drain — 10 ticks at firstMeowballFirstHitmark=129f + meowballHitmarkInterval=116f intervals, each 128% of absorbed-element ATK. Each hit grants +2 Energy (3.5s ICD). Not authored; team-element-resolution + meowball volley both deferred.
abilities.description:
Jahoda dashes toward her opponent, entering the Shadow Pursuit state upon contact. While in this state, Jahoda moves continuously and swiftly: If nearby opponents are affected by Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo, she will quietly convert her **Purr-loined Treasure Flask** to that element, gradually filling it. When the duration ends or the skill is used again, Jahoda drains the Purr-loined Treasure Flask and deals a single instance of Anemo DMG to nearby opponents. When the Purr-loined Treasure Flask is full, Jahoda immediately drains it, exiting the Shadow Pursuit state and dealing a more powerful instance of Anemo DMG.
If her dash fails to make contact with an opponent, Jahoda instead drops a Smoke Bomb at her location, dealing a single instance of Anemo DMG to nearby opponents.

Moonsign: Ascendant Gleam: When the Purr-loined Treasure Flask becomes full, Jahoda will not immediately discharge it. Instead, for a short duration, she steadily consumes the stored element inside and periodically fires Fluffy Meowballs at nearby opponents, dealing DMG of the corresponding element stored in the Purr-loined Treasure Flask. When a Fluffy Meowball hits an opponent, Jahoda regenerates 2 Elemental Energy. This effect can be triggered once every 3.5s.

abilities.name: Hidden Aces: Seven Tools of the Hunter
abilities.caveat: The robots' damage tick is gated on absorbing an enemy element AND requiring Moonsign Ascendant Gleam (≥2 Moonsign characters) — at Nascent Gleam (1 Moonsign char) the robots do not deal damage at all, only heal. The damage tick (172.66% ATK FlatDmg, absorbed element, ~2.33s interval) is not authored — it depends on team-element-absorption + Moonsign-team-state. The heal-tick scaling shown here covers the ATK% portion only; in-game heal also adds a flat heal portion (~1102 at lvl=10) which the schema's heal effect cannot express alongside scaling.
_curatorNotes: Initial burst hit at hitmark=0f (immediately): 259.0% ATK Anemo elemental burst.

Robots: 2 robots base (+1 with A1 Electro), heal active char every 1.45s (87f) for burstHealFlat + burstHealPP×ATK = 1101.7 + 143.77% ATK at lvl=10. Heal authored as scaling form (143.77% ATK); flat-heal portion ~1102 not representable in HealEffect schema.

Robot damage (Moonsign Ascendant Gleam only): 172.66% ATK FlatDmg of absorbed element, ~2.33s interval (140f base, ×0.9=126f with Cryo A1). Not authored — gated on team-Moonsign-Gleam + element absorption + onHit-from-summon (3 deferred primitives stacked).
Duration: burstDuration=790f = 13.17s. Authored on summons[].duration. Robots follow active char (combat.Player() targeted in robotAtkTick).
Burst frames: burstFrames=InitAbilSlice(48), ActionSkill=53 ActionAim=55 ActionDash/Jump=54 ActionWalk=55 ActionSwap=36. Per Q-spec swap/N/E/D/J — N defaults to animLen=48.
Cooldown: SetCDWithDelay(burst, 18*60, 1). ConsumeEnergy(13) drains 13 energy from teammates; not modelled.

A4 Sweet Berry Bounty (heal-on-active-with-HP>70% triggers +100 EM 6s on healed char): not authored as Effect — gating on heal-trigger + HP-state-of-target is two layers we don't track. Schema doesn't currently route heal events through Effect triggers.
C1 (50% Meowball bounce): RNG damage extension; not authored.
C4 (+4 Energy on robot element absorption): would need an absorption-event trigger; not authored.

C6 (Moonsign Gleam: when flask full, +5% CR / +40% CD to all Moonsign party for 20s): authored on the C6 node below as a buff effect with teamFaction:moonsign condition (note: teamFaction conditions currently evaluate to null at parse time per tier-c-guide).

passives.name: Plan to Get Paid
_curatorNotes: A1: Robot enhancement based on highest-count team element (Pyro: +30% robot DMG, Hydro: +20% heal, Electro: +1 robot count, Cryo: -10% interval). Determined at Init time from team composition. With C2 + Moonsign Gleam, also applies the second-highest element's enhancement (up to 2 active).

Each enhancement modifies a robot system field (robotAi.FlatDmg, robotHi.Src, robotCount, robotHitmarkInterval) — none are exposed as Effects in our schema. The robot system itself is partially authored on the burst as a summon with a heal effect; the A1 enhancements scale that heal/damage but in an element-resolved-at-init manner that doesn't fit any current trigger primitive.

Not authored — flagged. Effective gameplay: a Pyro-heavy team gets stronger robot damage; Hydro-heavy gets stronger heals; Electro gets a third robot; Cryo gets faster ticks. Document in user-facing release notes when buff rendering for Jahoda lands.
passives.description:
When your team has at least one Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo character, the **Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots** from the Elemental Burst Hidden Aces: Seven Tools of the Hunter will be enhanced based on the number of characters of each corresponding element.
Jahoda secretly keeps track of these characters. Among them, the element with the highest number of characters determines the enhancement effect:
· Pyro: Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots deal 130% of their original DMG.
· Hydro: Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots heal for 120% of their original healing amount.
· Electro: The number of Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots increases by one.
· Cryo: The attack interval of Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robots is reduced by 10%.

If there's a tie between elements, the order of priority that determines which enhancement takes effect is: Pyro, Hydro, Electro, then Cryo. Only one elemental effect can initially be triggered.

passives.name: Sweet Berry Bounty
_curatorNotes: A4: When a Robot heal triggers on active char with HP > 70%, +100 EM to that char for 6s. Three deferred primitives: (1) per-heal-event trigger; (2) HP-state condition on target; (3) the 'lowest HP off-field char' additional heal that the same A4 mechanic also fires. Not authored. The original stub had a self+manual buff effect — removed; replaced with description-only entry.
passives.description: When a **Purrsonal Coordinated Assistance Robot** from the Elemental Burst Hidden Aces: Seven Tools of the Hunter triggers healing on an active team member, if that character's HP is above 70%, their Elemental Mastery will be increased by 100 for 6s.
